title: I Built the Ultimate Chinese All-Road Bike

takeaways.text: Schwalbe G-One 700×40 tires (measured about 40 mm) on 26 mm-internal rims cleared the fork easily but had little room at the rear and rubbed the 2× front derailleur, so they had to go.
LightCarbon supplies shims that fit a Di2-style battery into the proprietary seatpost; hoses route through split spacers and a compression ring and were straightforward with a cable-pull trick.
Bontrager 700×38 all-round gravel tires, the official maximum, cleared the front derailleur and chainstays with modest room.
Despite the aero tubes it rides far more comfortably than expected on mixed surfaces, helped by the sloping top tube, dropped seatstays, 38 mm tires at about 40 psi and a tall head tube.
Longer trail and wheelbase make it very stable and easy to ride hands-free; the seatpost never slipped.
The build weighed 8.26 kg with pedals, bottle cage and computer mount (he estimates just under 8 kg without); total cost was about £2,121.

disclosure: LightCarbon supplied the frameset and wheels without payment and had no say in the content.
summary: Build and first rides of the size-58 LCR018-D as an all-road bike with L-TWOO ER9 2× and 26 mm-internal carbon gravel wheels.
